cases.situation: My roommate and I are fighting over text about dishes. I got sarcastic, she's getting angrier. I want to stop it before it blows up.
cases.reply: I don't want to keep doing this over text, and I'm sorry I got sarcastic. I get that you feel like you're the only one keeping the kitchen going. Can we talk tonight around 8 when you're home? You matter more to me than a sink.
cases.note: Reflect her feeling without conceding the facts; the facts get sorted at 8.

cases.situation: 跟老公因为今年过年回谁家在微信上吵起来了，他觉得每年都在迁就我家，越说越激动，我也说了他妈妈的难听话。想先停一下。
cases.reply: 我们先别在微信上吵了，刚才我说你妈那句话太冲了，对不起。我知道你觉得每年都是在迁就我家。今晚吃完饭我们好好聊，好吗？回哪家过年，都没有我们俩重要。
cases.note: 先认自己那一句的错，再说出对方的感受，最后给一个明确的时间继续谈。

cases.situation: My sister and I fought about who's hosting Mom's 70th. I said I needed a break and would call at 7, and she's sent 6 more angry texts since.
cases.reply: I'm not ignoring you. I said I'd call at 7 and I will. I just can't do this well right now.
cases.note: One line, then silence until 7. Answering each text restarts the fight.

cases.situation: Mi socio Martín y yo tenemos una cafetería en Valencia. Estamos discutiendo por WhatsApp si subir los precios en octubre, le dije que 'no tiene ni idea de números' y ahora está muy enfadado; dice que no valoro lo bien que conoce a los clientes. Quiero parar esto antes de que se complique.
cases.reply: Martín, nos estamos calentando los dos, y lo de que no tienes ni idea de números sobró. Lo siento. Entiendo que sientes que no valoro lo bien que conoces a los clientes. ¿Lo hablamos mañana a las 9, antes de abrir, con las cuentas delante? La cafetería es de los dos y quiero que la decisión también lo sea.
cases.note: Retirar la frase concreta que dolió, sin tocar todavía el tema de los precios, y fijar una hora para retomarlo.

cases.situation: A coworker, Dmitri, and I are going back and forth in our #launch Slack channel about delaying the release. He thinks it isn't ready and I called his concerns paranoid; he just wrote 'maybe read the spec before commenting'. The whole team is watching.
cases.reply: Dmitri, we're both getting heated and this thread isn't helping either of us. Calling your concerns paranoid was sharp, that's on me. I can see you're worried we'd ship something broken. Can we jump on a call at 3 today and post the decision here after?
cases.note: At work in public: own your part, reflect his worry, and move it to a call with a time and a promise to report back to the channel.

cases.situation: My 15-year-old, Zoe, and I are yelling in the kitchen about her coming home at midnight instead of 10. I told her she's 'acting like a spoiled brat'. She's crying and shouting back. I want to stop this right now, in person.
cases.reply: Okay. We're both really heated, and calling you a spoiled brat was out of line. I'm sorry. I can tell you feel like I don't trust you at all. We still need to talk about the curfew, but I need twenty minutes first. I'll knock on your door in twenty minutes and we'll talk properly. I love you, that part's not up for debate.
cases.note: Own the insult specifically, reflect her feeling without conceding the curfew, and say exactly when you'll come back.

cases.situation: My best friend Hana has been giving me one-word replies all day and just texted 'forget it, you clearly don't care'. I honestly don't know what I did. I don't want to get defensive.
cases.reply: I can tell you're really upset with me, and I don't want to brush past that. I'm not going to argue. I honestly don't know what I missed, and I want to. Can I call you at 8 tonight so you can tell me the worst part? You matter way too much to me to let this sit.
cases.note: When you don't know the cause, don't guess and don't defend: name her feeling, ask for the worst part, and give a time.

cases.situation: 昨晚女朋友面试完，我一直忘了问她结果，她生气了，我还说了句'你太敏感了'，吵起来。后来我说先冷静一下，今晚8点再好好聊。现在快8点了，第一句该怎么说？
cases.reply: 我想了一下昨晚的事。先说一句：'你太敏感了'这句话是我不对，对不起。我听到你的意思是，你面试完一直在等我问一句，我却一直没问，让你觉得你的事在我这里不重要。我理解得对吗？你说，我先听。
cases.note: 暂停之后准时回来，先认自己那句话，再复述你听到的，请她纠正；她说完之前不要解释。

cases.situation: My boyfriend Sam and I are fighting over text because the electric bill got a $35 late fee. I kept insisting he forgot to pay it, then I checked and it was my month. He's furious that I blamed him.
cases.reply: You're right, it was my month, and I was wrong to blame you. I'm sorry. I'll pay the $35 today and set a reminder so it doesn't happen again. Can we talk tonight when you're home?
cases.note: When you were simply wrong, skip the 'we're both heated' framing: own it plainly, fix it, and don't explain how you mixed it up.

cases.situation: My ex, Daniel, and I are fighting over text about who takes our daughter Lily to a birthday party this Saturday. I made a crack about his new girlfriend Hannah always being around and now he's furious and says my plans keep eating into his weekends. We'll be co-parenting for years and I want to stop this.
cases.reply: Let's stop doing this over text. The comment about Hannah was a cheap shot and I'm sorry. I get that you feel like my plans keep eating into your weekends. Can I call you at 8:30 tonight, once Lily's asleep, and we sort Saturday then? We both want her to have a good weekend.
cases.note: With a co-parent, the line about what's bigger than the fight is the child: own the jab, reflect his grievance, and put a time on the call.

cases.situation: 我爸72岁了，上个月倒车蹭了两次。刚才我在电话里劝他别开车了，说了句“你这样早晚出事”，他火了，说我咒他、把他当老人看，把电话挂了。想发条微信先缓一缓。
cases.reply: 爸，刚才电话里我话说得太冲了，“早晚出事”那句不该说，对不起。我知道你是觉得我把你当老人看，要把你的自由拿走。开不开车不用今天定，周六我回家吃饭，咱们当面慢慢聊。我就是太在乎你了。
cases.note: 跟长辈吵架，先认具体那句话，说出他真正在意的面子和自由，开车的事留到当面谈。

cases.situation: My wife Mel and I are arguing in the car about my mum staying with us for three weeks at Christmas, and I made a crack about her mum's visit last summer. We've got two more hours of driving to her parents' place and the kids are in the back with headphones on. I can't exactly walk away.
cases.reply: Mel, I don't want to do this in the car with the kids right behind us. Bringing up your mum's visit was a cheap shot, and I'm sorry. I can hear that three weeks feels like a lot to you. Can we park it until tonight, once the kids are in bed at your parents'? I'm on your side in this, even if it hasn't sounded like it.
cases.note: When you can't leave the room, pause the topic instead: agree a time, then talk about anything else until then.

cases.situation: My girlfriend Ines is in Lisbon and I'm in Toronto. We're fighting on WhatsApp because I missed our video call again, and I snapped 'I'm not your 24/7 support line'. It's almost midnight for her, she's upset, and I have a work meeting in ten minutes.
cases.reply: Ines, the 'support line' comment was unkind and I'm sorry. I know missing another call made you feel like you come last. It's nearly midnight for you and I've got a meeting in ten minutes, so can I call you tomorrow at 7pm your time, 2pm mine, and we talk properly? I love you, and that's not in question.
cases.note: Across time zones, give the return time in both zones so the pause reads as a plan, not as you rushing off to a meeting.

cases.situation: 大学室友五个人国庆去厦门，我和小林在群里因为民宿钱怎么AA吵起来了，她分到的房间最小，觉得按人头平摊不公平，我说了句“你每次都想占便宜”，另外三个人都不说话了。想先把火灭了。
cases.reply: 小林，我们别在群里吵了，“每次都想占便宜”那句是我说过头了，对不起。我知道你是觉得你那间房最小，按人头平摊不公平。今晚9点我给你打个电话，我们俩把账算清楚再发到群里。大家好不容易凑一起出去玩，别因为几百块坏了心情。
cases.note: 在群里当众吵，就在群里当众认那一句，具体的账挪到私下电话里算，再回群里给结果。

cases.situation: My downstairs neighbour Gary knocked at 10pm to complain about my kids running around, and I snapped 'maybe move to a house then'. He's still standing at my door and we're both getting louder. I want to calm it down right now.
cases.reply: Gary, we're both wound up, and the 'move to a house' comment was rude. I'm sorry. I can hear the noise has really been getting to you, especially late in the evening. Can I knock on your door tomorrow at 6 and we work out something about evenings? We're going to be neighbours for a long time.
cases.note: In person with a neighbour: own the one line, reflect the real grievance without agreeing to terms at the door, and set the time yourself.

cases.situation: My boyfriend Tom and I were arguing about money tonight, and when I raised my voice he threw a mug at the wall and stood in the doorway shouting. I left and I'm at my friend Ana's now. He's texting 'come home, we need to finish this'.
cases.reply: I'm safe at Ana's and I'm staying here tonight. When the mug hit the wall and you stood in the doorway, I got scared, so I'm not coming back to finish this tonight. If we talk, it'll be on the phone tomorrow at 6.
cases.note: Once things are thrown or someone blocks the door, safety comes before calming things down: you don't owe an apology to leave. If he threatens you or turns up, call emergency services; a local domestic-abuse helpline can help you think through what comes next.

cases.situation: At the pub tonight my friend Leo, who's had a few pints, started having a go at me for moving to Manchester next month and 'abandoning' the group. I snapped back that at least I'd had the guts to leave our hometown. We've been mates since school and I want to cool it down right now, not have the real conversation tonight.
cases.reply: Leo, that was a cheap shot and I'm sorry. I can tell you're gutted about me going, and I don't want to have this conversation badly over pints. Can we get breakfast tomorrow at 10 and talk properly? You've been my mate since school, and a move isn't changing that.
cases.note: When drink is involved, the pause is the whole job; do not try to settle anything tonight.

cases.situation: 我跟直属领导陈姐在企业微信上为四季度预算吵起来了。她担心四季度超支，要砍我的推广预算，我回了句“你根本没看我的方案”，她回“你这是什么态度”。我不想丢工作，也不想就这么放弃预算的事。
cases.reply: 陈姐，刚才那句“你根本没看我的方案”是我说过头了，对不起。我明白您担心的是四季度超支，这个顾虑我理解。预算的事我还是想当面把数字跟您过一遍，明天上午10点您有15分钟吗？
cases.note: 对上级：只收回那句冒犯的话，不收回立场，把争论搬到当面并给出具体时间。

cases.situation: Mein Sohn Felix (24) und ich streiten per WhatsApp, weil er sein Pflegestudium im letzten Jahr abbrechen will. Ich habe geschrieben 'Du ziehst nie etwas durch', und er antwortet, ich hätte ihm noch nie zugetraut, selbst zu entscheiden. Ich will das beruhigen, bevor es kaputtgeht.
cases.reply: Felix, ich höre jetzt auf, per Nachricht zu streiten. Der Satz, dass du nie etwas durchziehst, war unfair, und es tut mir leid. Ich verstehe, dass du dich von mir nicht ernst genommen fühlst, wenn es um deine eigenen Entscheidungen geht. Kann ich dich morgen um 19 Uhr anrufen und erst mal nur zuhören? Du bist mir wichtiger als jede Studienfrage.
cases.note: Die Studienfrage bleibt bewusst offen; heute geht es nur darum, aus dem Streit herauszukommen.

cases.situation: We're at my parents' house for Sunday lunch and my brother-in-law Rob and I have started arguing about immigration across the table. I told him he 'gets all his opinions from YouTube', and now we're both raising our voices while Mum looks upset and the kids are listening. I want to cool it down right now, in person.
cases.reply: Rob, let's stop, we're both getting loud and this isn't the place. The YouTube comment was a cheap shot, and I'm sorry. I can tell you feel I'm writing off your view without hearing it. If you want to pick it up properly, let's do it over a beer next Friday, just us. Today's about Mum's lunch.
cases.note: In front of family, the pause is the point; own the jab out loud so everyone at the table hears it.
